newsitem.title: USA: British tourist survives skydiving accident.
newsitem.headline: British tourist survives skydiving accident.

text.p: A novice British skydiver survived a 12,000-foot (3,650-metre) drop with a failed parachute because his instructor sacrificed himself to break the young man's fall, witnesses said on Tuesday.

Gareth Griffith, a 21-year-old management consultant from London, fractured his spine in the jump on Sunday when his parachute did not open properly and he landed on top of his instructor, a spokeswoman at Orlando Regional Medical Centre said.
Griffith, a tourist making his first jump, also suffered injuries to his abdominal organs and several broken ribs. The injuries were not life threatening and he was not paralysed, she said.
Instructor Michael Costello, 42, of Mount Dora, Florida, was killed in the fall.
Witness Lee Godwin said Costello saved his student by rolling at the last moment to take the brunt of the fall.

"An experienced skydiver's never going to lose his cool because it's not impossible to survive a fall like that," Lee Godwin said. "Mike kept his cool and did what he had to save his student. That was Mike."
An instructor for 18 years, Costello was jumping in tandem with Griffith, a common practice for veterans jumping with novices, said Costello's business partner, Wilma Godwin.
After the two left their Cessna Caravan airplane, their main parachute deployed but failed to open, according to police reports. A backup parachute was deployed but also failed.
Lee Godwin said the chutes became entangled and the two men went into a violent tumble, which Costello corrected, leaving him on top and Griffith on the bottom.
Shortly before they hit, perhaps less than 100 feet (30 metres) from the ground, Costello drew in his arms and legs and rolled so that he hit the ground first with Griffith on top of him.
Costello was killed instantly, according to a police report. Griffith was taken by helicopter to Orlando.

The two were jumping into a field next to the rural airport in Umatilla, Florida, about 30 miles (48 km) northwest of Orlando. Griffith and five friends were enrolled in a two-week skydiving course, Wilma Godwin said.
